intent.raw: Set up a research strategy for DOMAINSPEC-LANGUAGE-HANDOFF.md that maps reusable DomainSpec Core and Arcanum material and explores a category-theory-oriented language for contracts, rules, DomainSpec taxonomy, and Arcanum taxonomy.
intent.objective: Produce a governed research route that can discover existing reusable artifacts, model a small formal language around contract/schema/iteration objects, and prepare a design package before parser implementation.
intent.operator_sentence: Start the DomainSpec language as a category-theory language focused on contracts, rules, DomainSpec taxonomy, and Arcanum taxonomy while mapping what DomainSpec Core already provides.

techniques.purpose: Treat contracts, schemas, rules, examples, validators, and iteration records as typed objects and morphisms before choosing syntax.
techniques.validation_note: Every categorical term must map back to a concrete DomainSpec or Arcanum artifact path and must remain an explanatory model until decision-gate approves language semantics.

technique_overlays.trigger: The user wants a category-theory language focused on contracts, rules, DomainSpec taxonomy, and Arcanum taxonomy.

techniques.purpose: Model semantic contract composition before syntax selection.
techniques.validation_note: Must produce concrete mappings such as contract object, schema object, validator morphism, example fixture, lifecycle state, and iteration delta.

technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The model must cite repository artifacts and avoid inventing formal vocabulary that cannot be grounded in DomainSpec Core or Arcanum surfaces.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The research problem has separable evidence lanes: DomainSpec source taxonomy, Arcanum capability taxonomy, contract/schema examples, and formal language modeling.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Parallel role-bound research can map existing artifacts faster while keeping the parent route responsible for synthesis and promotion guardrails.
context: projects/domainspec-language/DOMAINSPEC-LANGUAGE-HANDOFF.md asks for design only, not parser implementation.
projects/domainspec-language/CONTEXT-PACK.md already identifies initial evidence but does not exhaust DomainSpec Core or Arcanum taxonomy surfaces.
The category-theory framing needs critique from both formal-model and repository-evidence perspectives.

roles.purpose: Map existing DomainSpec Core artifacts for contracts, schemas, taxonomies, relationships, constitutions, templates, and validators.
Map Arcanum sigil, spell, formulae, dispatch, invoke, refine, task-session, inventory, ontology, and glossary surfaces.
Extract reusable contract/schema/ledger/example/validator patterns from Craft, dispatch-spec, invoke handoff, and task-session evidence.
Stress-test the category-theory framing and identify where it clarifies composition versus where it risks obscuring validation authority.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Approve running role-bound subagents for the DomainSpec language research lanes before execution.

steps.name: Read handoff and confirm non-implementation boundary
stop_conditions: Block if the route starts implementing a parser before design package approval.
Flag if Craft becomes the canonical language scope instead of one fixture.

steps.name: Map reusable DomainSpec Core and Arcanum evidence

capability_metadata.validation_note: Used as a research inventory lane; canonical validator set does not currently list inventory.

inputs.ref: repo paths for arcanum, implementation/domainspec, sigils-library, docs, projects

stop_conditions: Flag any evidence claim without a concrete path.
Block promotion if a generated install surface is treated as canonical source without owner confirmation.

steps.name: Frame category-theory contract language model

techniques.purpose: Distill contracts, schemas, rules, validators, examples, taxonomies, and iterations into composable typed objects and transformations.
techniques.validation_note: The frame is valid only when each formal concept maps to existing DomainSpec or Arcanum evidence.

stop_conditions: Flag formal terms that are not needed to explain contract composition or validation authority.
Block if category theory language replaces the concrete DomainSpec artifact model instead of clarifying it.

steps.name: Crosswalk DomainSpec taxonomy and Arcanum taxonomy

capability_metadata.validation_note: Used as a research crosswalk lane; canonical validator set does not currently list ontology-vault.

stop_conditions: Flag ambiguous concepts that share names but have different owners.
Block if the crosswalk claims ontology promotion authority.

steps.name: Synthesize language design package outline
stop_conditions: Flag if contract, schema, and iteration are not separated.
Flag if lifecycle states and validation authority are unnamed.

steps.name: Record syntax and authority decisions

capability_metadata.validation_note: Used for explicit route decisions; canonical validator set does not currently list decision-gate.

stop_conditions: Ask if choosing YAML-first, DSL-first, or dual-surface syntax would affect implementation commitments.
Block implementation if validation authority remains unresolved.

steps.name: Validate route and name first fixtures
stop_conditions: Flag if fixtures include Craft only.
Block if validation claims promotion readiness without implementation work pack approval.

steps.name: Prepare implementation work-pack handoff
stop_conditions: Defer implementation until the design package, syntax decision, and fixture plan are accepted.
Block if parser implementation starts before the handoff criteria are met.

gates.condition: No parser, validator implementation, or syntax lock-in before the design package and decision gate exist.
Research claims cite concrete paths or explicit unresolved candidates.
The route does not promote inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or language semantics without owner review.
First validation fixtures include Craft plus at least one non-Craft fixture such as dispatch-spec or invoke handoff.
Subagent fanout requires explicit operator permission before execution.

boundaries.contract: Arcanum artifacts may be mapped as evidence, but lifecycle/promotion authority stays with their owning sigil, spell, formulae, or framework package.
Recommended subagent fanout remains permission-gated and is not executed by this dispatch artifact.

authority.validation: dispatch-spec validator for route shape; future language validator only after work-pack approval
authority.evidence: repository-local concrete paths and bounded research receipts
authority.memory: Codex memory visibility only; no automatic knowledge promotion

receipts.producer: role-bound research lane or parent route

state_namespaces.write_policy: Research artifacts, route receipts, and handoffs for this language lane only.
Read-only evidence during this route unless a later owner-approved task-session changes scope.
Read-only evidence during this route unless a later owner-approved task-session changes scope.

promotion_splits.target: Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or language canonical contracts
promotion_splits.rule: Research evidence can recommend promotion candidates but cannot promote them without explicit owner review.

promotion_guardrails: This dispatch designs a research route only.
No parser implementation starts before the language design package and decision gate exist.
No Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or language semantics are promoted by execution evidence alone.
Category-theory terminology is exploratory until mapped to concrete DomainSpec and Arcanum artifacts.
stop_conditions: Stop if the route begins implementation before design and decision artifacts are produced.
Stop if evidence cannot be grounded in concrete repository paths.
Stop if the category-theory framing cannot explain contract/schema/iteration separation better than the existing handoff model.
